entries.title: CvUnit combat bonus vs different ideology is not serialized
entries.mechanism: m_iCombatBonusVsDifferentIdeologyModifier is accumulated by changeCombatBonusVsDifferentIdeologyModifier (promotion/policy effects) and read by GetCombatBonusVsDifferentIdeologyModifier in combat strength, but it is absent from CvUnit::read, CvUnit::write and CvUnit::reset. After any load the field is 0 on the machines that loaded, while machines that played continuously keep the accumulated value.

evidence.quote: void CvUnit::read(FDataStream& kStream)  (field absent here, in write at 22068 and in reset at 961)
[3] nonser.member CvUnit.h:1611 CvUnit::m_iCombatBonusVsDifferentIdeologyModifier not in Write (not in Read)

entries.trigger: A unit carries the ideology combat bonus and fights a unit of a different ideology after a hot-join or reconnect (only the joiner loads), or after any save/load compared with continuous play. A full resync heals it, because every peer, the host included, reloads.
entries.symptom: Combat damage differs; CvUnit HP (FAutoVariable) diverges and the exe raises OOS. In the lab: continue run differs in ext field m_iCombatBonusVsDifferentIdeologyModifier, then in CvUnit damage.

impact.note: Mid/late game only (ideologies). Reconnects are common in Lekmod MP, so the joiner-side divergence is realistic.

entries.proposed_fix: Keep the save format: recompute the field in CvUnit::read from the unit's promotions (and the owner's policies, if a policy feeds it) after the promotion set is loaded; also zero it in reset.

trap.idea: continue run from a state with the bonus promotion and a pending combat; lockstep hot-join variant once lockstep-sim exists

entries.title: CvPlayer::m_bCanChooseReformationBelief starts from garbage
entries.mechanism: The bool is serialized but never set in the CvPlayer constructor, reset() or init(). In a new game it holds whatever the heap held (and, in a warm process, the previous game's value, since CvPlayer objects are reused). CvReligionClasses reads it to decide whether a player who founded a religion may add a reformation belief.

evidence.quote: kStream >> m_bCanChooseReformationBelief;  (so a load overwrites the garbage)
[3] uninit.member CvPlayer.h:2045 never set in ctor/reset/init; serialized, so garbage only until first load

lekmod6, golden-hyg, 100 turns, civhost --heap-fill 0x00 vs 0xFF / 0x01 / 0xA5: player segments differ from turn 1 (CvPlayer::Write m_bCanChooseReformationBelief, offset 276 of every player segment, 0x00 -> 0xFF), game/map/team segments diverge from turn 83 in all three fills

same runs on det-hyg-fix2 (golden-hyg + LEKMOD_HEADLESS_FIX_0002, the member initialised to false): no game/map/team divergence for 100 turns, only the player segments (other garbage fields, DS-0023..DS-0026) differ

entries.trigger: New game (not a load). A player with garbage true who founds a religion: an AI adds a reformation belief early on one machine only; a human gets a reformation notification on one machine. Warm process: carries over from the previous game. Reproduced: lekmod6 turn 83 under any non-zero heap fill; not reproduced in pangaea6 or continents8 within 100 turns (no religion founder with the flag set in those games).

entries.title: static processPlayerAutoMoves in CvGame::updateMoves
entries.mechanism: A function-level static latches whether human auto-moves may run. It is not saved and survives between games in one process. It is reset to false whenever an AI (barbarians and city-states included) is processed, which happens every turn on every peer.

evidence.quote: [2] static.local CvGame.cpp:9186 function-level static persists across turns/games, not saved

entries.trigger: Hot-join or reload during the human auto-move phase of a turn (joiner starts with false while others are latched true), or a warm process that ended the previous game with the latch set.
entries.symptom: Human auto-moves (queued multi-turn moves, automated units) run in a different update slice on the joiner; ordering of unit moves within the turn can differ.

impact.note: Window is one turn phase; the per-turn AI reset bounds it.

entries.proposed_fix: Make it a CvGame member, reset in CvGame::reset and on load (or derive it from synced player state each call).

trap.idea: lockstep-sim hot-join at the start of the auto-move phase; warm vs fresh process

entries.title: m_bReceivedFirstMission / m_bMPOrderedMoveOnTurnLoading are not serialized
entries.mechanism: GAME_ALLOW_ONLY_ONE_UNIT_MOVE_ON_TURN_LOADING flags. They are set on every peer by the net handlers (ResponsePushMission and friends) and reset at turn start (CvGame.cpp:8410) and in init (CvGame.cpp:426), both only when GAMEOPTION_FIRSTMOVE is set, and they are not saved. They gate only whether the local client may send further selection-list commands while the turn is loading.
entries.trigger: Hot-join or reload in the first seconds of a turn: the joiner may send (or block) one extra command.
entries.symptom: No direct simulation divergence (sender-side gate only); at worst a command that others accept arrives in a different order.

impact.note: Gate on command sending, not on command execution.

entries.proposed_fix: Initialise both in CvGame::reset; treat them as UI state (no serialization needed).

trap.idea: lockstep-sim hot-join while the turn is loading, with a scripted first-move command

entries.title: Stop-converting / stop-digging promises recorded only on the asking human's machine
entries.mechanism: DoFromUIDiploEvent runs on every peer (ResponseDiplomacyFromUI). For FROM_UI_DIPLO_EVENT_HUMAN_DISCUSSION_STOP_SPREADING_RELIGION and _STOP_DIGGING, SetPlayerAskedNotToConvert/Dig and SetPlayerAgreeNotToConvert/Dig are inside if (bActivePlayer), so only the asking human's machine records the request and the AI's answer. IsStopSpreadingReligionAcceptable / IsStopDiggingAcceptable themselves are deterministic (no RNG, no active-player use). The agreed-not-to-convert flag feeds AI missionary targeting (CvReligionClasses.cpp:6762, 6972; the prophet reader at 5631 is compiled out because its AUI define sits in a commented block of _Defines.h); the dig flags have no simulation reader in the DLL (only Lua UI), so the digging half diverges saved state only.

entries.mechanism: CvDealAI::DoTradeScreenClosed is called from UI Lua (Player:DoTradeScreenClosed) on the human's machine only. It calls ClearDealToRenew (clears CvDeal::m_bConsideringForRenewal and the AI's deal-to-renew) and may DoCancelWantsResearchAgreementWithPlayer. Both are synced state: DoAcceptedDeal checks GetDealToRenew at line 193 and calls PrepareRenewDeal on the peers that still hold it.

entries.title: Half-timer air-patrol / paradrop rule reads the local wall clock in synced mission code
entries.mechanism: CAN_SET_INTERCEPT_HALF_TIMER / CAN_PARADROP_HALF_TIMER make canAirPatrol / canParadropAt return false once getTimeElapsed()*2 > turn length. getTimeElapsed returns m_fTimeElapsed, which each machine fills from its own clock (hasTurnTimerExpired). The checks run inside synchronous mission validation and execution (CvUnitMission::CanStartMission / ContinueMission) on every peer, so near the half-time mark, after a reconnect (the joiner's timer restarts) or after a pause/unpause (StartWithOffset(getTimeElapsed()) uses each peer's local value), peers disagree whether the mission is legal.
entries.trigger: Turn timer on, GAMEOPTION_FAST_HAND on, pitboss turn time 0 or GAMEOPTION_RELATIVE_TURN_TIMER (AUI_GAME_RELATIVE_TURN_TIMERS is on); a human orders air patrol or paradrop close to half the turn time, or any time after a reconnect or a timer pause.
entries.symptom: Unit activity/position diverges (FAutoVariable on CvUnit), exe OOS; AI callers (CvTacticalAI, CvMilitaryAI) run at turn start and are rarely affected.

impact.note: Competitive Lekmod MP commonly uses turn timers; reconnect makes the window a whole half-turn.

entries.proposed_fix: Evaluate the time rule only on the sending client (UI/command validation) and skip it in synchronous execution, or send a synced 'half-time passed' event from the host and test that flag instead of the clock.

trap.idea: turn-timer scenario with FAST_HAND; peers with clock_offset straddling half-time; scripted air-patrol command; expect CvUnit mission/activity divergence

entries.title: CvCityStrategyAI yield-delta arrays: uninitialised and not serialized, read by worker scoring
entries.mechanism: m_asBestYieldAverageTimes100 / m_asYieldDeltaTimes100 are value-initialised only under AUI_WARNING_FIXES (off in the golden defines), are not in Read/Write, and are refreshed only by UpdateBestYields, which is called from CvBuilderTaskingAI::Update in the owner's setTurnActive. ScorePlot multiplies by GetYieldDeltaTimes100 of the plot's working city. A city founded mid-turn, or every city after a load (hot-join, reload), holds heap garbage until the owner's next turn start.

entries.title: Consulates catch-up handler removes itself (handler set differs after load)
entries.mechanism: Lekmod_OnAdoptConsulates removes itself from GameEvents.PlayerAdoptPolicy after the first Consulates adoption. Peers that played continuously no longer have the handler; a peer that loads (hot-join, reconnect) re-registers it at context load. A later Consulates adopter in Industrial+ gets catch-up league votes only on the loaded peers.

entries.proposed_fix: Do not remove the handler; the policy-id test already filters other policies.

entries.title: Mexico UA reveal handler removes itself
entries.mechanism: lekmod_mexico_ua (PlayerDoTurn) reveals city-state cities within 10 tiles of Mexico's start and then removes itself. After a load the handler is back on the loaded peers and runs again on Mexico's next turn there only. With one Mexico the re-run is usually a no-op (cities already revealed); with two Mexicos, or a city-state city that appeared later, the reveal state diverges.
entries.trigger: Two Mexico players, or a new city-state city in range, plus a hot-join/reload.
entries.symptom: Plot revealed bits diverge (silent; AI decisions may follow).
entries.proposed_fix: Run the reveal once per Mexico player at game start from a synced event, without removing the handler (or keep a per-player done flag in saved data).

trap.idea: continue run with two Mexico players

entries.title: Dummy policies granted from a local engine event (Events.SequenceGameInitComplete)
entries.mechanism: Events.SequenceGameInitComplete fires on each machine when its own load completes, including on a joiner only. The handler calls SetNumFreePolicies(1), SetNumFreePolicies(0) and SetHasPolicy for players lacking the dummy policy. It is guarded by HasPolicy, so it is idempotent except that SetNumFreePolicies(0) would zero pending free policies of a player who still lacks the dummy policy (for example player 0, skipped by ipairs).
entries.trigger: Hot-join/reload while some eligible player lacks the dummy policy and has pending free policies.
entries.symptom: Free-policy counts or policy set diverge on the joiner.
entries.proposed_fix: Grant dummy policies from a synced hook at game start (or in the DLL at player init), not from Events.*.

trap.idea: continue run with a civ that has a dummy policy and a pending free policy at the save point

entries.title: CvPlayer::disconnected mutates simulation at network-event time
entries.mechanism: disconnected() is called by the exe when the network layer reports a drop, not as an ordered game command. It switches the slot to SS_COMPUTER (AI takeover), and with GAMEOPTION_AI_GIMP_NO_DEALS cancels deals, closes embassies, cancels research agreements, evacuates diplomats and calls verifyUnitValidPlot. Each peer applies this at its own point in the command stream.
entries.trigger: A human disconnects while other peers are mid-turn or mid-command-stream (incident 04 class).
entries.symptom: Deals, embassies and unit positions differ for a window; AI takeover runs AI logic for the slot on some peers earlier than others.

impact.note: Disconnects are common; whether the exe serialises the callback with the command stream is unknown (needs lockstep-sim).

entries.proposed_fix: Have the host issue the takeover and the deal cancellation as an ordered net command, and do only UI work in disconnected().

trap.idea: lockstep-sim with a scripted drop at different command offsets per peer; compare deals and unit plots

entries.title: GAMESTATE_OVER set only on the eliminated active player's machine
entries.mechanism: CvGame::update sets the game state to GAMESTATE_OVER when the local active player is dead and not an observer. Game state is synced data; the other peers keep GAMESTATE_ON.
entries.trigger: A human is eliminated in MP and stays connected (worst case: the host).
entries.symptom: That peer stops normal turn processing; if it is the host, the next resync save carries GAMESTATE_OVER.
entries.proposed_fix: In network MP, switch the eliminated player to observer/defeat UI without changing the synced game state.

trap.idea: scenario where a major is eliminated; active_player = that major vs another; compare CvGame game state

entries.title: Gameplay Lua is loaded as UI contexts from InGame.lua
entries.mechanism: All Lekmod gameplay scripts (GameEvents handlers that mutate synced state) are started by ContextPtr:LoadNewContext calls in the DLC's InGame.lua. A peer whose InGame.lua comes from another UI mod (EUI or an older install that overrides the file) never registers those handlers, and every handler-driven change diverges. Checked 2026-10-17 (the EUI-vs-UI profile comparison (civsim.detlab.euiui diff)): this does not happen from the EUI choice itself. ui_check.bat installs the same InGame.lua (tmp\ui\InGame.lua.ignore) for EUI and non-EUI players, EUI's own InGame.lua loses the skin lookup to Lekmod's (package priority 250 < 300), and the 37 gameplay contexts plus their includes (40 names) resolve to identical files in both profiles. The risk remains for an install where ui_check.bat did not run (Lekmod only shows reminders: the LegalScreen text and the chat line JoiningRoom sends, TXT_KEY_UI_CHECK_BAT) or a third mod that overrides the file.
entries.trigger: Peers whose InGame.lua is not Lekmod's (ui_check.bat skipped, an old install, another mod overriding it); EUI vs the bundled UI alone is not enough.
entries.symptom: Immediate divergence on the first Lua-driven event (dummy buildings, policies, civ UAs).

impact.note: Install-dependent; no code path in one install is wrong.

entries.title: AI decisions depend on the x87 precision-control setting of the game-core thread (24-bit diverges from turn 42-44)
entries.mechanism: The simulation is bit-exact for x87 precision control 53 and 64 bit but not for 24 bit. The first call where a 24-bit run differs from the 53-bit run (lekmod6, turn 43, CityDoTurn zone) is 'Choosing city build from Top Choices' (CvWeightedVector<CvCityBuildable>::ChooseFromTopChoices) with a different weight sum (623 vs 440), i.e. the city production weights already differ. That path does floating-point decisions that are truncated or rounded to integers: ReweightByTurnsLeft = int(double(weight) / pow(turnsLeft, factor)), IsYieldDeficient = round(double average * 100) compared with round(desired * 100). A 24-bit mantissa moves such values across an integer or .5 boundary. The exact flipping expression is not isolated (the diag RNG log names the first affected decision, not the arithmetic); the two listed are the candidates found in that path (the exp() maintenance factor at CvCityStrategyAI.cpp:1005 is compiled out under the golden defines).

evidence.quote: civhost --fpu-pc 24 vs 53 (per Update slice), 100 turns: first divergent turn 44 lekmod6, 43 pangaea6, 42 continents8; --fpu-pc 64 identical to 53 in every run
RNG log lekmod6 turn 43: first differing call is 'Choosing city build from Top Choices', range 623 (53-bit) vs 440 (24-bit)

with FIX-0017 (FPU_PRECISION_GUARD) --fpu-pc 24 and --fpu-pc-global 24 are insensitive on lekmod6/pangaea6 (100 turns); without it --fpu-pc 24 diverges at turn 44 (game, map, player03) and --fpu-pc-global 24 at turn 1 (map)

entries.trigger: Two peers whose game-core threads run at different x87 precision control. Direct3D 9 without D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE leaves the creating thread at 24 bit, Direct3D 11 does not touch it: a DX9 / DX11 mixed lobby is the candidate (fidelity risk D10). Not triggered when all peers use the same exe. Unknown whether the real game-core thread is ever affected.
entries.symptom: AI production and diplomacy decisions flip around turn 40 (earlier on bigger maps); game, map, teams and players diverge afterwards; exe OOS from the first different random call.

impact.note: Every mixed lobby if the premise holds; zero otherwise. Mechanism confirmed by the fpu_pc axis; whether a real game-core thread is ever at 24 bit still needs a reverse-engineering check of which thread creates the D3D9 device and a probe of the x87 control word at a real CvGame::update entry. FIX-0017 pins 53 bit / nearest at every exe entry into the DLL, so peers running that build no longer depend on it.

entries.proposed_fix: Pin the precision in the DLL: _controlfp_s(&cw, _PC_53, _MCW_PC) at the entry of CvGame::update (or once per game-core thread start), and/or make the three expressions precision-independent (integer arithmetic for the deficiency test, explicit double rounding).

entries.title: CvWorldInfo save/sync omits EstimatedNumCities: warmonger penalty 0 after a load
entries.mechanism: CvWorldInfo::writeTo/readFrom (version 2) serialize every Worlds column except EstimatedNumCities, which BNW added and only CvDiplomacyAIHelpers::GetWarmongerOffset reads (iWarmongerOffset = 1000 * Estimated / (cities on map * cities remaining)). CvPreGame::read restores s_worldInfo with operator>>, which keeps the member's previous value; worldInfo() re-caches from the database only when the world size ID differs, so it never repairs it. In a fresh process the value is 0: every conquest or liberation after the load adds 0 warmonger, while the continuous game adds the full amount. A peer that loads (resync, reconnect, MP reload) holds 0 or whatever its previous pregame cached, so its CvDiplomacyAI opinions, approaches and the sync RNG stream drift from the other peers at the next conquest. The MP lobby syncs s_worldInfo with the same operator, so clients can also start a new game with another value than the host.

impact.note: CvDiplomacyAI state is outside the exe sync check until an AI decision consumes RNG differently. Also a single-player balance bug: a reloaded game forgives conquests.

entries.proposed_fix: Re-read EstimatedNumCities from the Worlds row of the loaded world size ID in CvWorldInfo::readFrom (and readFromVersion0). Save format unchanged.

entries.title: CvTacticalAI::m_Postures (last turn's zone postures) is not serialized: posture hysteresis lost on load
entries.mechanism: UpdatePostures picks each dominance zone's posture with SelectPosture(pZone, eLastPosture), where eLastPosture comes from m_Postures, the previous update's result. Several branches are sticky (STEAMROLL, SIT_AND_BOMBARD, EXPLOIT_FLANKS, ATTRIT_FROM_RANGE, COUNTERATTACK continue while a weaker condition holds), so a posture can persist for many turns. CvTacticalAI::Write stores only a phony int and m_TempZones; m_Postures is neither saved nor rebuilt, so after a load every zone starts from AI_TACTICAL_POSTURE_NONE and may pick another posture. The posture selects the tactical moves (and their order) of every AI and city-state.

entries.title: EUI NotificationPanel adds a CITY_TILE notification only on the owner's machine (GameEvents.CityBoughtPlot handler)
entries.mechanism: The EUI variant of Lekmod's NotificationPanel (Lua\tmp\eui, copied to Lua\UI by ui_check.bat for players with EUI) registers GameEvents.CityBoughtPlot inside Events.SequenceGameInitComplete. The DLL fires that hook on every peer from CvCity::DoJONSCultureLevelIncrease (border growth by culture), but only peers that have this file run the handler, and it acts only when playerID is the local active player: g_activePlayer:AddNotification(NOTIFICATION_CITY_TILE, ...). CvNotifications::Add records for human players only, so the EUI owner's machine appends an entry (text, turn, lookup index, ring end index; the 100-slot ring also evicts older entries sooner) that no other peer has. The list is serialized in the player segment (CvNotifications::Write) but is not an FAutoVariable, so the exe OOS check does not see it; simulation code reads it only through DS-0018 (IsNotificationExpired). The standard NotificationPanel has no such handler and the DLL adds no CITY_TILE notification itself. What decides is whether the OWNER has EUI: EUI on the other peers changes nothing (the handler is a no-op for other players and for AI players), so a lobby where everybody has EUI is affected exactly like a mixed one. The same kind of local-only entry is added by EUI's CityView when a production queue item is removed (NOTIFICATION_PRODUCTION, a click path).

evidence.quote: lockstep, 3 peers, human slot 0, verbatim handler: control equal for 60 turns; EUI on the owner's peer (or on all peers): only the player00 segment diverges, from turn 5 (the border growth) to turn 60, written by CvNotifications::Write (cvnotifications.cpp:311), peers 1 and 2 identical to the control run

entries.trigger: A human player with EUI whose city grows its border by culture (every few turns per city, in practically every game). Mixed EUI/non-EUI lobbies and all-EUI lobbies are equally affected; only a lobby with no EUI owner is clean.
entries.symptom: The owner's player segment (notification list) differs from every other peer's copy of that player from the first border growth on; no other segment differs, the exe OOS check is silent. It turns into a desync only through a sim read of the list (DS-0018).

impact.note: The difference exists in nearly every EUI game but nothing in the simulation reads the list except DS-0018's flag clear. A busy EUI owner fills the 100-slot ring faster (one entry per border growth), which widens DS-0018's window.

entries.proposed_fix: Make every install produce the same list: remove the CityBoughtPlot handler from Lekmod's tmp\eui NotificationPanel and add the CITY_TILE notification in the DLL (CvCity::DoJONSCultureLevelIncrease, for the human owner, on every peer), or keep the toast out of the serialized list. Independently remove the sim write from IsNotificationExpired (DS-0018). For multiplayer lobbies today: no action needed unless GAMEOPTION_NO_MP_POLICY_SAVING and a turn timer are on; then prefer lobbies where nobody uses EUI.

entries.title: UI getters recompute and store the lazy might cache: Player:GetMilitaryMight() from Lua writes FAutoVariables on the asking machine only
entries.mechanism: CvPlayer::GetMilitaryMight, GetEconomicMight and getPower are lazy caches: when m_iTurnMightRecomputed < elapsed game turns the first caller of the turn recomputes m_iMilitaryMight / m_iEconomicMight from the current units, gold and population and stores all three through a const_cast. The three are FAutoVariables (sync archive, serialized). Player:GetMilitaryMight() is exposed to Lua unchanged, so a UI script on one machine can be the first caller of the turn. Demographics.lua (stock screen, Lekmod's edited copy) calls it for players 0..MAX_MAJOR_CIVS in BuildTables(), at context load and every time the screen is shown. The AI refreshes the caches of the major civs every turn (CvDiplomacyAI, CvPlayer.cpp:31473 replay data), so for them a UI call finds a current cache and writes nothing. Unused player slots and most city-states are not asked by anyone, so the UI call writes them: lockstep with one peer asking at turn 10 diverges from turn 10 in the segments of player06..21 and of 10 of the 12 city-states, with the other two peers identical to the control run. The source comment at CvMinorCivAI.cpp:8526 ("Don't recalculate within a turn, can cause inconsistency") shows the lazy cache is known to be order dependent. Found while checking EUI vs the standard UI; identical in both profiles (only Demographics and the base game's WhosWinningPopup call these getters).

entries.title: A human's UI move order runs a path search on that machine only; the shared IgnoreUnits pathfinder then gives other danger values there (CvDangerPlots, CvCity::m_iThreatValue)
entries.mechanism: CvGame::selectionListGameNetMessage is the UI path of every human move or attack order (right-click in the exe, Game.SelectionListGameNetMessage in Lua) and runs only on the ordering player's machine, before the command is sent. For GAMEMESSAGE_PUSH_MISSION it calls CvUnit::CanSwapWithUnitHere to choose between sendSwapUnits and sendPushMission, and CanSwapWithUnitHere runs GC.getIgnoreUnitsPathFinder().DoesPathExist (GeneratePath with bReuse = true; the AUI turn-limited variant is compiled out, all AUI_ASTAR_* defines sit in the commented block of _Defines.h). That finder is a global shared with synced code: CvDangerPlots::AssignUnitDangerValue (UpdateDanger, inside the MP-cache-safe window of CvPlayer::setTurnActive) calls GeneratePath(..., bReuse = true) on it and divides the unit's strength by the turns-away of the last node. In network MP the UI search itself is not reused (discardCacheForMPGame) and SetMPCacheSafe(true) forces a reset when the window opens, yet the one extra local search changes later results on that machine: one unit's danger contribution doubles or halves (turns-away 1 vs 2; sums 400 vs 801, 650 vs 1051, 0x14 vs 0x29 per plot). Which finder member carries the state was not isolated; the non-AUI reset clears only the nodes on the open and closed lists (CvAStar.cpp:305-322), so node data outside both lists survives (hypothesis, not verified). CvDangerPlots is serialized but not sync-checked; UpdateDanger also stores GetCityDanger in CvCity::m_iThreatValue for every city of the player, an FAutoVariable, so for a player with cities the difference reaches the exe's City sync check. Values are recomputed every turn, so the state re-converges unless a decision consumed it first (keep-going rerun: equal again at turn 59). Stock Lekmod code: the UI-order fuzz reproduces it on v-golden-hyg.

The DLL also exports CanSwapWithUnitHere to the exe (CvDllUnit.cpp:214); whether the exe calls it on hover was not checked.
entries.symptom: CvDangerPlots of some player differs on the ordering human's machine (silent); for a player with cities CvCity::m_iThreatValue differs too: exe 'City out of sync' and a resync. AI tactical and homeland decisions that read danger can diverge before the next recompute.

impact.note: Every human move order is a trigger; seen without any deliberate probe in 3 of 8 multi-human v-release sessions in 120 turns plus one campaign B session. Self-healing per turn, so most cases are one resync; a consumed difference (an AI move) persists.

entries.proposed_fix: Keep UI-side path queries off the global finders that synced code uses: give the UI call of CanSwapWithUnitHere in selectionListGameNetMessage (and other UI path helpers such as Player:GetRecommendedFoundCityPlots) its own CvIgnoreUnitsPathFinder instance, or save and restore the finder state around them. Alternatively make every synced search independent of history (clear all nodes on a non-reused search, as the AUI_ASTAR_MINOR_OPTIMIZATION reset does); that changes AI play as well.

entries.title: Commands execute in arrival order: under network delay each machine runs its own command before remote ones, so RNG use and synced state interleave differently per machine
entries.mechanism: Every Response* handler executes its command when the engine delivers it; nothing in the DLL orders the commands of different players, or a command relative to the AI's turn processing. In the lockstep harness a sender gets its own message one frame after sending and, with --remote-delay D, the other machines get it D frames later (the exe also runs a sender's own command through the network loopback). Two humans' RNG-using commands, or one human command and the AI turn processing (both draw from the jon stream), then run in a different order on different machines. Seen: lek6s2 turn 37 jon call 213 is CvMinorCivAI::DoTeamDeclaredWarOnMe (a human declared war on a city-state: the 'Become Wary Of aggressor roll') on peer 0 but CvUnit::getCombatDamage (the other human's attack) on peer 1; lrg10s1 turn 23 call 202, the wary rolls interleave with the diplomacy AI. Downstream writers: CvPlayer::Write (unit damage dealt/taken counters, FAutoVariables), CvMinorCivAI friendship and wary arrays, CvEconomicAI m_aiExplorationPlots, CvPlot visibility count and revealed owner. Three of the delay sessions diverged with identical RNG streams (plot visibility, exploration plots on the human's own peer); those are order effects on non-RNG state or another local cache, not separated. Real only if the exe executes commands in arrival order without a global per-slice order (NetTurnSlice gating is not modelled in civhost); if the exe orders commands per slice, this is an artifact of the delay model. The replay-log order (mask candidate) is the benign form of the same mechanism.

entries.title: Player:CalculateGoldRate / CalculateInflatedCosts from Lua refresh the serialized CvTreasury unit-maintenance cache on the calling machine only
entries.mechanism: CvTreasury::CalculatePreInflatedCosts stores m_iExpensePerTurnUnitMaintenance and m_iExpensePerTurnUnitSupply (plain ints, serialized by CvTreasury::Write) as a side effect of computing the costs. It runs from CalculateInflatedCosts and from CvPlayer::calculateGoldRateTimes100 -> CalculateBaseNetGoldTimes100; both are exposed to Lua (Player:CalculateGoldRate, Player:CalculateInflatedCosts) and called by TopPanel, EUI tooltips, TradeLogic and DiploRelationships on one machine. DoGold recomputes the fields every turn, so the difference is transient (keep-going run: turns 1, 2 and 25 of 30). Readers: CvEconomicAI::DisbandExtraWorkers, CvMilitaryAI::DisbandObsoleteUnits and the World Congress vote logic run in doTurnPostDiplomacy (CvPlayer.cpp:5163) before DoGold (5264), so an AI player whose cache one machine refreshed through the UI (a tooltip, the trade screen with that AI) after its unit count changed could take a different disband decision there. That path was not reproduced.

entries.title: City:GetNextBuyablePlot / City:CanBuyPlot() from Lua draw from the synced game RNG on the calling machine
entries.mechanism: CvCity::GetNextBuyablePlot picks one of the cheapest buyable plots with getJonRandNum(iListLength, "GetNextBuyablePlot picker"), the synced game RNG. Lua exposes it as City:GetNextBuyablePlot() and through City:CanBuyPlot() with no arguments (lCanBuyPlot calls GetNextBuyablePlot and then dereferences the plot without a NULL check, a crash when nothing is buyable). A UI script calling either on one machine advances the jon stream there only: the diag RNG log shows the extra call (range 1) on the calling peer, every later jon call shifts, and AI decisions diverge (CvGrandStrategyAI rolls, areas, plots). No installed Lekmod or EUI UI file calls them (the UI uses GetBuyablePlotList and CanBuyPlotAt), so only a mod or an edited UI file triggers it.

entries.title: Plot:GetFoundValue from Lua fills the serialized m_aiFoundValue cache on the calling machine only
entries.mechanism: CvPlot::getFoundValue fills m_aiFoundValue[eIndex] (plain int array, serialized by CvPlot::write) when it holds -1; Lua exposes it unchanged (Plot:GetFoundValue). AI players refresh their entries every turn (AI_updateFoundValues); for humans AI_doTurnPre returns early, so a value a UI call filled stays different on that machine for the rest of the game. The only simulation reader is CvPlayer::GetBestSettlePlot (AI players, their own entries) and the value is a deterministic function of the plot, so the difference is value-consistent: the serialized state differs, decisions do not. No installed UI file calls GetFoundValue.

entries.title: AI deal offers to a human check the deal against each machine's local player instead of the human it is for
entries.mechanism: CvDealAI::DoEqualizeDealWithHuman(pDeal, eOtherPlayer, ...) passes GC.getGame().getActivePlayer() to IsDealWithHumanAcceptable instead of eOtherPlayer (both calls). It is reached from the trade screen (local, the active player is the deal's human) and from the AI's own turn on every peer: IsMakeOfferForLuxuryResource / OpenBorders / ResearchAgreement / Embassy towards a human. There, IsDealWithHumanAcceptable's 'no gold in the deal and within one GPT' shortcut reads pDeal->GetGoldTrade(local player): on the target human's machine the human's gold items, elsewhere another player's (none), so the offer decision and the statement logged in the AI's diplomacy log can differ per machine. The peace-treaty branch also tests IsPeaceTreatyTrade(local player).
